_note: Joint catalog for the fired-unit kit. Rule 1: fired clay only ever bears in compression -- no clay hook ever carries tension (Japanese joints turn tension into bearing on a hooked face, and the hook's neck is where timber splits; in clay it would shatter). Rule 2: small, replaceable, non-rusting keys and wedges do the locking and the pulling-tight, and can be re-driven. Sources: rock/RESEARCH_NOTES.md (joinery section). All sizes [TO-MEASURE] in Phase R.

unit_locator.name: shallow drafted locator keys
unit_locator.force_path: keys stand ~1 mm short of bearing, so they only stop units sliding while stacking; load bears on ground rim bands of the shells and webs; shear by friction under the rod clamp (mu 0.48-0.62)

panel_clamp.name: rod clamp (komisen / shachi-sen draw, in steel)
panel_clamp.after: komisen draw-pin: pulls the joint shut and can be driven out
panel_clamp.force_path: 2 rods in open cells pre-compress every bed joint; disc springs hold the force as joints seat; re-torque from the top channel at any time; rods sit loose in 60 mm cells so rust can never burst the clay (the lesson of the Acropolis's steel-in-concrete repairs); 316 stainless for a long-life build

panel_fold.name: wedged key at the fold (shachi-sen style)
panel_fold.after: shachi-sen paired wedges; kanawa-tsugi wedge pre-compression; nuki wedges 1-2 mm oversize
panel_fold.key: fired-clay key block (large, compression only) + tapered wedge pair (316 stainless or titanium; hardwood only if dry and replaceable), 3 per fold
panel_fold.force_path: the wedge pair draws the two panels' edge units onto the key block: clay in compression only; wedges driven 1-2 mm oversize to pre-compress, with ~3 mm of travel left to re-drive later; in an earthquake the joint slips by friction and re-seats (energy out by friction, never by breaking clay)

base_slider.name: friction slider with dowel stops at the plinth
base_slider.after: Greek column-drum dowels and empolia (shake tests: rocking and sliding, little residual offset)
base_slider.force_path: panel bears on the plinth through the bottom channel; stainless dowels in oversized sockets stop large slip; small slip dissipates energy

ring_splice.name: bolted splice plate across each fold
ring_splice.after: Poleni's iron hoops on St Peter's; the Armadillo Vault's tension ties
ring_splice.force_path: the dome's rim thrust becomes ring tension in the panels' top channels; it crosses each fold through a bolted plate: in plain sight, re-tightenable

dome_course.name: seat step + radial bearing faces
dome_course.after: Brunelleschi's herringbone (stops inward sliding ring by ring); Inca through-wall keying
dome_course.force_path: each voussoir's lower bed has a small ledge whose seat is no steeper than atan(mu/1.5) ~18-22 deg, so a dry unit rests on it in compression and friction; the main joint faces are radial, carrying the dome's thrust in compression; no clay hooks

dome_key_course.name: closing key voussoir
dome_key_course.after: keystone; recursive interlocking puzzles (one key part placed last locks the set)
dome_key_course.force_path: the last unit of each course is slightly tapered and pressed in to close the ring; from then on hoop compression holds every unit of that course
